rules.title: NJ Law Against Discrimination: source of lawful income protection in housing
rules.requirement: Landlords may not discriminate in housing based on the source of lawful income or source of lawful rent payment a tenant uses. For example, a landlord cannot refuse to rent to a Section 8 HUD voucher holder based solely on that source of income.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to the rental of all real property, with exceptions for renting one unit of an owner-occupied two-family dwelling and renting rooms in an owner-occupied one-family dwelling.
rules.exemptions: Rental of a single apartment in a two-family dwelling where the owner occupies the other unit; rental of rooms by the owner or occupant of a one-family dwelling they occupy; religious-organization preference for same-religion persons; familial-status protection does not apply to housing for older persons (N.J.S.A. 10:5-5mm).

rules.penalty: Complaint to the Division on Civil Rights within 180 days of the violation, or a Superior Court action within two years.
